summary.short: FDA regulation classifying over-the-counter photoplethysmograph analysis software that identifies irregular heart rhythms as Class II (special controls). It requires clinical, software, non-clinical and human factors testing and specified labeling. The text states no effective date.
summary.long: Section 870.2790 identifies a photoplethysmograph analysis software device for over-the-counter use. The device analyzes photoplethysmograph data and provides information for identifying irregular heart rhythms, and is not intended to provide a diagnosis. The device is classified as Class II (special controls). The special controls require clinical performance testing of the detection algorithm under anticipated conditions of use; software verification, validation and hazard analysis, with documentation of the software's technical specifications; non-clinical testing of signal-quality detection; and human factors and usability testing showing that users can correctly use the device from the labeling alone and interpret its output. Labeling must include hardware platform and operating system requirements, situations in which the device may not perform at an expected level, a summary of clinical performance testing, a description of what the device measures and outputs, and guidance on interpreting results. The provision sets no enforcement regime and states no effective date.
